The classification overview must not be treated as a uniform care chain for every member, and the conditions are verified against the target specialty, jurisdiction and actual position.

Editorial observation suggestion: first verify the professional education and qualification conditions of the target direction, then understand the actual tasks, records and collaboration requirements; if clinical work is involved, also verify fine manipulation, patient communication and protection training. Observing preferences does not replace professional ability or licensure.

Editorial verification suggestion: programme length, qualification examination and training requirements are first verified against the programme; for clinical positions, exposure, protection, posture and operating conditions are verified separately. Hand or visual limitations must be assessed specifically, and no individual is excluded by occupational name nor promised lower requirements in another direction; work beyond authority must be handled according to policy.

Decision center: first choose a specific direction and verify its objects, outputs and lawful authority; clinical, reporting and population prevention cannot all be combined into one patient care plan.

About 78% of BLS2025 dentists broad group employment is in dental offices and 12% self-employed; some work alone, in small teams or in partnership. The clinical, reporting or public health tasks and hours differ by position; the protection, posture and equipment described on this page are editorial clinical examples and do not generalise contact frequency for the broad group.

Similar names do not mean the same authority: this page takes the perspective of the occupation of dentists as a whole (U.S. SOC 29-1020 broad group), in which general dentists (29-1021.00) provide diagnosis and treatment of common oral disease; orthodontists (29-1023.00), oral and maxillofacial surgeons (29-1022.00) and prosthodontists (29-1024.00) each have their own occupational code and specialty training requirements, and specialties not listed separately fall under 29-1029.00; dental hygienists (29-1292.00) perform licensed examination and scaling, dental assistants (31-9091.00) provide chairside assistance, and dental laboratory technicians (51-9081.00) fabricate restorations in the laboratory to prescription. The specific scope of practice follows one's own practice qualification, registration scope, specialty training and unit authorization, and is not inferred from the occupational name.

Inputs that must be verified: chief complaint and present illness, systemic disease, medication and allergy history, intraoral examination and imaging findings, previous oral treatment records, and the patient's ability to pay and conditions for attending. What must not be done: do not provide care without practice qualification or beyond registration scope, do not perform irreversible procedures on experience when evidence is insufficient, do not omit informed consent and medical records, and do not omit instrument sterilization, isolation and radiation protection procedures.

Fit judgments should combine clinical mentoring observation, case discussion and patient feedback, and are not replaced by an interest type or a single test; manual dexterity, image interpretation ability, tolerance in communicating with patients in pain or anxious, and the ability to keep up record habits over the long term must all be confirmed in real training and feedback.

All paper exercises on this page use fictitious materials; real examination, anesthesia and prescribing, radiological examination and surgery, and medical record and privacy handling are carried out by licensed and registered physicians under the applicable jurisdictional regulations (such as mainland China's Physicians Law and the practice requirements for the dental category, and U.S. state licence requirements) and unit policies; specialty procedures also require the corresponding specialty training and authorization.

The objects of a clinical position may include the chief complaint, intraoral examination findings, previous treatment and medication history, and the outputs may include a lawfully formed treatment plan, medical records, prescriptions and follow-up records; this is an editorial clinical example. BLS lists pathology, imaging report and public health directions separately, and every member of the broad group cannot be required to complete the same patient care chain. The specific objects, outputs and authority are verified against the direction, jurisdiction and unit policy.

Check one: whether the information is complete — whether the chief complaint, history, medication and allergy history, imaging and previous treatment have been verified in full; missing items must be pursued with the patient or supplemented by examination, and irreversible procedures must not begin on impressions.

Editorial verification question: is the diagnosis supported by intraoral examination and imaging materials, and are there missing items or contradictions that require an authorized physician's confirmation, additional examination or consultation? The paper exercise does not judge treatment, symptom control or irreversible procedures on its own.

Editorial clinical verification: explain the condition and the measures, and for surgery and special examinations or treatments give specific disclosure of risks and alternatives and obtain explicit consent under the applicable rules; article 25 of China's Physicians Law distinguishes general disclosure from the explicit consent required for surgery, special examinations and special treatments.

Check four: whether the procedures are within one's own practice scope and ability — whether anesthesia, prescribing, extraction, root canal treatment or surgery fall within one's registration scope and trained ability; when beyond it, involve a supervising physician according to the process or refer to the corresponding specialty.

Check five: whether isolation, protection and equipment conditions are adequate — whether isolation such as rubber dam, instrument sterilization procedures, personal protection and imaging protection are carried out according to standards and whether equipment is in usable condition.

Check six: whether postoperative instruction, recall and records form a closed loop — whether postoperative precautions, medication, recall timing and the situations requiring immediate attendance are explained and recorded, and whether anomalies and adverse events are reported as required.

2025 broad group: dental offices 78%, self-employed 12%, government excluding state and local education and hospitals 2%, outpatient centres 2% and physicians' offices 2%; the remaining 4% is an editorial difference rather than official other. The clinical posture and exposure verification on this page is an editorial example, not a survey frequency for the whole broad group.

This page uses editorial clinical examples to illustrate three work areas: receiving and examining patients, authorized procedures, and records and follow-up; specific directions may involve care, imaging or pathology reports, population prevention, research or teaching, and it cannot be said that every member of the broad group completes the same chain. The objects, outputs, authority and equipment are verified against the actual specialty; broad-group duties in BLS are not a uniform task table for every position.

Where are the boundaries between the occupation of dentists as a whole and general dentists, the dental specialties, dental hygienists, dental assistants and laboratory technicians?

This table compares the dentists broad group, the specialties and adjacent occupations by objects, basis, process, outputs, responsibility, collaboration and boundaries. BLS2025 general dentists are the largest subcategory; the objects of each specialty and U.S. training requirements differ. The work and authority of hygienists, assistants and technicians must be verified separately by jurisdiction, and diagnosis is not prohibited across the board nor the workplace restricted by name. The broad group includes clinical, reporting and public health directions, and the comparison table is not a uniform task or training path for every member. Insufficient evidence: this page did not obtain a broad-group-specific AI task score or a reliable SOC/ISCO research correspondence. The ILO exposure index is not an adoption rate, automation rate or job loss probability; no broad-group score is given, and subcategory scores are not used to fill in.
Core purpose

Diagnose and treat patients' oral health, unifying prevention, preservation, restoration and functional maintenance within a single treatment plan, and taking responsibility for clinical outcomes and patient safety.

Core purposes of the subcategories and adjacent occupations: general dentists provide diagnosis and treatment of common oral disease; orthodontists correct malocclusion; oral and maxillofacial surgeons perform surgery for maxillofacial disease and trauma; prosthodontists provide complex prosthodontics and occlusal reconstruction; dental hygienists perform licensed examination, scaling and preventive procedures; dental assistants provide chairside assistance; dental laboratory technicians fabricate restorations to prescription.
Main objects and basis

The objects are the patient's oral health status, chief complaint and previous treatment records; the basis is oral care standards and guidelines, infection control and radiation protection requirements, drug and material instructions, and the unit's clinical policies.

Objects and basis of the subcategories and adjacent occupations: general dentists focus on common oral disease (general dental practice standards); orthodontists on dentofacial malocclusion and growth (orthodontic standards); oral and maxillofacial surgeons on maxillofacial disease and trauma (surgical standards and surgical authorization); prosthodontists on missing teeth and occlusion (prosthodontic standards); dental hygienists on periodontal care and prevention (oral prevention standards and state licensure); dental assistants on the treatment process (infection control requirements); and laboratory technicians on work orders and impression or scan data (prosthetics process requirements).
Core process

Consultation and history verification → intraoral examination and image interpretation → diagnosis and treatment plan → informed consent → performing procedures under isolation and protection → records and prescriptions → postoperative instruction and recall follow-up.

Processes of the subcategories and adjacent occupations: examination, management and recall for common conditions (general dentists); impression and image analysis and appliance design (orthodontists); preoperative assessment and surgery (oral and maxillofacial surgeons); preparation, impressions and restoration fitting (prosthodontists); examination, scaling and preventive procedures (dental hygienists); chairside assistance and instrument handling (dental assistants); prescription-based fabrication and inspection of restorations (laboratory technicians).
Main outputs
Diagnosis and treatment plan, informed consent, completed procedure and medication records, postoperative instruction, recall and follow-up records, and any necessary referral or return notes.

Outputs of the subcategories and adjacent occupations: records of diagnosis and treatment of common conditions (general dentists); treatment plans and stage-by-stage recall records (orthodontists); surgical and postoperative follow-up records (oral and maxillofacial surgeons); restoration and occlusion records (prosthodontists); periodontal examination and scaling records (dental hygienists); treatment assistance and sterilization records (dental assistants); restoration and inspection records (laboratory technicians).
Responsible party

The personnel in this occupation are responsible for the diagnosis, treatment plan and procedural quality, informed consent and medical records; matters involving other specialties must be handled by the corresponding specialty physician according to the process, and one's own authorization must not be interpreted expansively.

Responsible parties of the subcategories and adjacent occupations: general dentists are responsible for the diagnosis and treatment of common oral disease; orthodontists, oral and maxillofacial surgeons and prosthodontists are each responsible for decisions within their specialty; dental hygienists are responsible for examination and scaling within their licence; dental assistants are responsible for chairside assistance and instrument handling; laboratory technicians are responsible for the quality of restorations fabricated to prescription.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with other physicians in the hospital or clinic, dental hygienists, dental assistants, the laboratory and the imaging and laboratory testing links; when cases exceed one's practice scope or ability, or there are infection control hazards or equipment anomalies, pause the procedure, review the records and consult, refer or report according to policy.

Collaboration of the subcategories and adjacent occupations: general dentists collaborate with the departments and the laboratory; orthodontists and oral and maxillofacial surgeons collaborate with imaging, anesthesia and ward teams; prosthodontists collaborate with the laboratory; dental hygienists collaborate with dentists and patients; dental assistants collaborate with dentists and the front desk; laboratory technicians collaborate with physicians and quality staff.
Conclusion boundaries

This page is on the basis of the occupation as a whole: the U.S. SOC 29-1020 broad group combines general dentists and the dental specialties in its statistics, so the figures and descriptions on the page reflect this broad group rather than any one practitioner's daily work; an individual's actual work content depends on their scope of practice and whether they have completed specialty training.

The licence scope, preparation levels and regulatory requirements of the subcategories and adjacent occupations cannot be applied to other people on this page; specific requirements must be verified item by item against the target jurisdiction's official materials, specialty rules and the employing unit's policies.

Clinical scenario verification questions: how are the diagnostic evidence, missing history items, one's own scope, and the jurisdiction, statistical basis and work environment each verified? The six items below are explained next to the main text; these verification questions are not a uniform clinical task for the whole broad group.

Common misunderstandings include treating “dentist” as a single kind of position and ignoring the enormous differences between general dentists and the specialties within the same broad group; assuming that a degree is enough to practise and ignoring U.S. state licence requirements and mainland China's dental category physician qualification examination and practice registration; assuming that the figures in an occupational classification equal an individual's income and entry difficulty; mixing the duties of adjacent occupations such as scaling, chairside assistance and laboratory fabrication into the duties of dentists; and equating “dentists earn well” directly with stable take-home income, ignoring self-employment costs and the structure of specialty clinics. Each is explained below.

Verify the chief complaint, present illness, systemic disease, medication and allergy history, previous oral treatment records and imaging, and fill in missing items before developing a treatment plan.

Complete the intraoral examination and image interpretation, form a diagnosis and treatment plan, and explain the expected outcome, course of treatment, costs, risks and alternatives to the patient and obtain informed consent.

Perform anesthesia and procedures under isolation and protection, prescribing medication or commissioning the laboratory to fabricate restorations when necessary, and record each procedure and medication.

Cases beyond one's practice scope or ability are handed to a supervising physician or referred according to the process, errors and adverse events are reported truthfully, and authorization is not expanded on one's own.

Collaborate with physicians inside and outside the clinic, dental hygienists, dental assistants, the laboratory and patients according to responsibilities, communicate the condition, plan, costs and timelines truthfully, and complete medical records and infection control records.

When job hunting, also verify the target unit's actual service recipients, position authority and premises requirements; U.S. employer distribution is not used to infer Chinese institutional shares.

The editorial quality check selects the diagnostic basis, record explanations, procedural protection and subsequent feedback according to the actual direction; it is not the same clinical assessment for every member of the broad group.

Dentists (U.S. SOC29-1020 broad group) include general dentists 29-1021, oral and maxillofacial surgery 29-1022, orthodontics 29-1023, prosthodontics 29-1024 and other specialists 29-1029. BLS describes oral care and prevention and introduces the pathology, imaging and public health directions separately; the actual tasks are not all the same. In the United States a licence from the target state is required, and specialty training is verified against local requirements; the qualification and registration of dental category physicians in China follow Chinese rules, and the two countries' classifications and licences are not treated as precisely equivalent.

Examples for the maxillofacial surgery and prosthodontics directions: the former treats oral and maxillofacial disease or trauma surgically and produces surgical and follow-up records; the latter diagnoses, designs and fits dental restorations and produces prosthodontic plans and clinical records. Training and authority are verified separately and cannot be combined into one process.

Dental hygienists examine the mouth and provide preventive care under jurisdictional licensure and produce care and examination records; dental assistants support care, instruments and administrative processes under authorization and supervision. Their specific authority follows the state or jurisdiction, and U.S. codes are not used to infer Chinese licensure.

Dental laboratory technicians fabricate and repair restorations to prescription and specification and produce finished products and inspection records; manufacturing and clinical responsibility are borne separately, and laboratory fabrication cannot be treated as clinical diagnosis.

The U.S. SOC29-1020 broad group includes general dentists and the specialties; the specific objects may be clinical patients, pathology and imaging reports or population prevention, and the outputs are determined by the direction and authorization. The broad-group definition is not a uniform operating list for any one physician.
Direction within the occupation: general dentists (29-1021.00, the largest subcategory in the broad group)

Complete consultation and examination and image interpretation, manage common caries, pulpal and periodontal problems, perform fillings, root canal treatment, extractions and basic restorations, provide preventive guidance and regular recalls, and refer cases beyond one's scope to the corresponding specialty.

General dentists handle a variety of oral needs, while orthodontics, maxillofacial surgery and prosthodontics each have different objects and training; this page did not obtain a uniform study comparing procedure duration, equipment cost or case breadth, so no ranking is given.
If you want to cover common oral problems, become the patient's first contact point and take on first-contact and referral responsibility, general dentistry can be the starting point.
Direction within the occupation: orthodontists (29-1023.00)

Assess dental, jaw and facial growth and development, develop treatment plans, adjust step by step with fixed or removable appliances, arrange long-term recalls and post-treatment retention, and explain the course of treatment and cooperation requirements to patients and parents.

Orthodontics involves malocclusion appliances and follow-up; U.S. specialty training is verified separately. The occupational name cannot prove that no cutting is needed or that treatment time or equipment investment is lower than in other specialties; individual procedures follow lawful authority.
If you are willing to track the same group of patients over the long term and can judge progress from subtle changes across successive recalls, consider the orthodontic direction.
Direction within the occupation: oral and maxillofacial surgeons (29-1022.00) and prosthodontists (29-1024.00)

Surgery and prosthodontics are respectively surgical and prosthetic reconstruction roles, and are not combined into the broad group's technical complexity end. U.S. specialty training in BLS usually takes 2—4 years, with oral and maxillofacial surgery usually 4—6 years; this is not a Chinese duration or a ranking of the longest of all directions.

If you clearly want to perform surgery or complex functional reconstruction, plan directly along the education and training path of the corresponding specialty rather than treating training in another direction as a substitute.
Adjacent occupations: dental hygienists (29-1292.00) and dental assistants (31-9091.00)

Hygienists perform oral examination and preventive care within the specific jurisdiction's licence scope; assistants support care within the scope of licensed authorization and supervision. Their authorization is verified separately from a dentist's diagnosis, prescribing and procedural authority, and it cannot be inferred uniformly nationwide what a code authorizes or prohibits.

If you prefer preventive care and patient education, compare dental hygienists; if you prefer supporting the treatment process and accept working under a dentist's direction, compare dental assistants.
Adjacent occupation: dental laboratory technicians (51-9081.00)

Technicians fabricate and repair restorations to prescription, with manufacturing quality separate from the physician's clinical decisions. A technician identity cannot be used to infer that they absolutely never contact patients, nor can manufacturing skill be treated as lawful practice authority.
If you prefer independent fabrication, craft and precision verification without facing patients directly, you can compare the laboratory direction.
Boundary note: the relationship between the occupation as a whole, the subcategories and the specialties

U.S. SOC 29-1020 is a broad group that combines general dentists and the dental specialties in its statistics, so the wage and employment figures on the page reflect the broad group as a whole; the dental specialties not listed separately (29-1029.00) are a residual category whose practice content is determined by the specialty direction involved. Any attempt to infer individual authority from the occupational name does not hold.

When choosing, look at the actual path of undergraduate education and specialty training (whether residency or specialty training must be completed), the licence requirements of the target jurisdiction, and whether the institution has the corresponding diagnosis and treatment subjects and equipment.
Directions within the dentists broad group compared with adjacent occupations

The table below compares the main directions within the dentists broad group with adjacent and related occupations across the same set of dimensions: career direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which choice is a better fit. The directions within the broad group are used only to explain differences and do not mean that the same practitioner may practise across directions; the specific scope of practice follows one's own practice qualification, registration scope, specialty training and unit authorization.

Direction choice should depend on the types of cases and responsibilities you are willing to take on long term, not on the classification name or a single wage figure; the training duration, equipment investment and practice scope of the directions within the broad group differ greatly, and the qualifications and duties of adjacent occupations cannot be applied directly.

Comparison basis: the U.S. BLS Occupational Outlook Dentists broad group (position composition and entry descriptions) and the O*NET-SOC profiles of each subcategory (general dentists 29-1021.00, orthodontists 29-1023.00, oral and maxillofacial surgeons 29-1022.00, prosthodontists 29-1024.00, dental specialties not listed separately 29-1029.00, dental hygienists 29-1292.00, dental assistants 31-9091.00 and dental laboratory technicians 51-9081.00); used only to explain duty and training boundaries and not representing a uniform position design across employers.

Moving into dentistry from an adjacent occupation requires making up professional education and physician examination registration by jurisdiction, or a U.S. state licence, with clinical ability and specific specialty training verified separately. Short rotations cannot replace authority, and the same residency pathway is not fixed for all Chinese specialties.

Editorial inference: in an approved environment, software can assist with organizing patients' chief complaints and histories, flagging suspicious areas in images, comparing recall records, generating draft patient education materials, or assisting the shape design of intraoral scan data; this is a description of technical capability, not adoption-rate or effect evidence for this occupation.
Technical capability, actual adoption, job outcomes and replacement probability are four different questions; this page does not pass one off as another.

It can assist in generating imaging prompts, record summaries and draft follow-up data compilations, but these must be checked item by item against the intraoral examination, original images and oral care standards before being used for diagnosis and treatment decisions.

High-risk failures include treating imaging software marks as a diagnostic conclusion, missing lesions outside the field or negative findings, confusing patients and tooth positions, using unchecked medication or material information, and writing a software suggestion directly as a treatment decision.

Human control points are confirming patient identity and tooth position, verifying examination and imaging evidence, making the diagnosis and treatment plan, obtaining informed consent, performing procedures, managing complications, and deciding whether to recall, refer or transfer to a specialty.
If the unit has no explicit data permission, logging, validation, training and anomaly escalation processes, personal trials should not be treated as formal adoption.

BLS describes clinical care, pathology or imaging diagnosis and population prevention as different directions, and the clinical chain on this page is an editorial example that does not uniformise every member's tasks. The May 2025 broad-group median is 176,110 USD per year and 84.67 USD per hour, with the lowest 10% below 89,100 and the highest 10% above 337,210 USD; the five subcategory median comparison is not broad-group percentiles. 2025 employment 161,400, 2025—2035 growth 6% and 4,800 openings per year on average including replacement, which cannot be used to infer individual opportunity or AI effects. U.S. education and state licensure, Chinese physician qualification and registration, and the specific training and institutional filing are verified separately. Insufficient evidence: the NBS2025 consulted did not provide an oral occupational wage distribution, and this page did not obtain broad-group AI effects, specific task scores or a representative Chinese recruitment sample.
